title: Ingestion and Streaming Services: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Ingestion and Streaming Services: Visual Guide

1. Move Once Or Stream | five requirements tapped against the earlier migration services and this lesson's three streaming services, answered as state, ordering, replay, scaling and ownership, plus sliders for outage length against source log retention | a one-time move ends while a stream never does, and Datastream's recovery is bounded by the source database's log retention, not by anything Google manages

2. Copies Not Cursors | a topic fanning out to analytics, alerting and archival subscriptions, with a slider for analytics instances and a toggle that moves alerting onto the shared subscription | each subscription gets its own copy and cursor, so sharing one between two different applications silently makes them compete instead of each receiving all events

3. Ack And Redelivery | acknowledgement placed before or after the durable write, an exactly-once toggle, and five injected failures reporting lost, duplicate or safe | at-least-once plus an ack after the durable effect costs at most a duplicate, while exactly-once covers redelivery of one message ID and never a duplicate publish or an external database write

4. Workers That Cannot Help | a Dataflow job taking 10,000 events per second with sliders for max workers and available parallelism, plus hot-key, quota and sink-limit toggles that name the binding constraint | more workers help only when the work can be split, so parallelism, a hot key, a quota or the downstream sink can leave backlog growing while CPU stays low

5. Kafka Or Pub/Sub | seven comparison dimensions shown side by side with a self-managed versus managed Kafka toggle | the awareness-level comparison is about ownership and semantics rather than speed, and a managed Kafka service changes only the ownership row, never the programming model
